title: Distributed sliding-window boundary misalignment leads to enforcer overcount and regional 429 spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a regional autoscaling event on 2026-03-01 we saw repeated short-duration 429 storms for a subset of multi-tenant customers. Root cause analysis points to a sliding-window counter implementation where window boundary alignment between gateway replicas and the central counter store became inconsistent during instance rotations and a transient time adjustment, causing per-tenant counts to be double-applied for a small number of windows. This ticket captures the postmortem, immediate mitigations, and longer-term fixes to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Between 2026-03-01 08:12 UTC and 2026-03-01 08:46 UTC: five production clusters in us-west experienced 2-8 minute bursts of elevated 429s affecting ~12% of active API keys. Client-visible symptom: sudden request rejections with X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 despite apparent low request volume. No data loss or PII exposure. Several customers opened support tickets and some integrations briefly failed. Total estimated lost successful requests: ~38k.
root_cause: The enforcer uses local sliding-window counters on gateway replicas that periodically flush aggregate deltas into a sharded Redis counter store. During a short NTP-driven clock adjustment on a host pool and concurrent autoscaling-induced replica churn, some gateways advanced to the next window earlier than others while also re-sending buffered deltas for windows they believed were incomplete. A race in the flush logic permitted duplicate application of deltas across boundaries when a shard rebalanced concurrently. The combination of boundary misalignment + flush deduplication gap resulted in double-counted tokens for affected tenants, triggering premature quota exhaustion and 429 responses.
timeline: 2026-03-01 08:10 UTC - Autoscaler launched 3 additional gateway replicas in us-west due to a legitimate traffic uptick.
2026-03-01 08:11 UTC - A minor NTP adjustment (sub-second) occurred on a subset of hosts during image rotation; several gateways moved their window offsets by ~600ms.
2026-03-01 08:12 UTC - Monitoring alert: per-tenant 429 rate increased above anomaly threshold on us-west cluster (pager triggered).
2026-03-01 08:13-08:20 UTC - Incident responders confirmed 429s correlated with specific API key prefixes; rolled traffic and began mitigation.

2026-03-01 08:21 UTC - Emergency mitigation: reverted the sliding-window optimization PR (gateway runtime flag rollback) and disabled asynchronous flush retries to Redis. 429 rates declined within 2 minutes.
2026-03-01 08:30 UTC - Hotfix deployed to add idempotency tokens to flush messages and short-term gating on shard rebalances.
2026-03-01 08:46 UTC - Incident declared resolved; post-incident monitoring in watch mode for 24h.
immediate_mitigation: Rollback feature flag: disable gateway-side aggressive window advance optimization (flag: sliding_window_advance_v2=false).
Disable async flush retry path that could replay deltas without idempotency anchors.
Apply temporary rate-limiter soft-fallback: when a tenant crosses threshold due to counter inconsistency, fallback to conservative local allowance instead of hard 429 for up to 30s.
Notify affected customers via support with incident summary and ETA for permanent fix.
long_term_action_items: ENG: Add idempotency tokens and monotonic window IDs to all delta flush messages; persist last-applied-ID per shard to prevent duplicate application (owner: Marco Chen, estimate: 5).
SRE: Harden shard rebalancer to quiesce flush pipelines during slot migration or provide transactional apply semantics (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 8).
Infra: Ensure NTP/chrony config is uniform and perform a focused audit/chaos test for minor clock shifts under autoscaling (owner: DevOps, estimate: 3).
QA: Create integration test that simulates interleaved window advances, instance churn, and shard rebalances to catch double-counting regressions (owner: QA, estimate: 5).
Product: Re-evaluate rate-limiter telemetry to emit per-tenant diagnostic keys that include window-ID hashes to help faster triage (owner: Product Observability, estimate: 3).
Docs: Update runbook with clear rollback knobs and an automated mitigation playbook for sliding-window anomalies (owner: Oncall Docs, estimate: 2).
verification_plan: Deploy idempotency tokens to staging and run synthetic test harness for 24h with induced clock jitter and autoscaler churn.
Promote to canary subset in us-west with increased telemetry sampling; verify no duplicate-applied deltas via last-applied-ID metrics.
If canary stable for 48h, roll out to remaining regions with gradual rollout policy and 30m watch windows.
metrics: Peak 429 rate (us-west): +4200% above baseline during burst window.
Affected API keys: ~12% of active keys in cluster; heavy-weight customers saw 1-3 minute request interruptions.
Time to mitigate (rollback + soft-fallback): 9 minutes from alert to visible decline.
No increase in 5xx or data-plane latency attributable to mitigation steps.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial RCA draft completed. We should prioritize idempotency + shard quiesce before any further performance micro-optimizations.
2026-03-03 - Marco Chen: Implemented idempotency token PoC and added last-applied-ID persistence in the test harness. Observed no duplicate applies in 1000-run simulation.
2026-03-05 - Priya Rao: Proposed change to rebalancer to add a drain phase; requires coordination with infra team for maintenance windows.
2026-03-08 - DevOps: Completed NTP config audit; found 3 host pools with aggressive polling config — these were aligned and scheduled for policy enforcement.
2026-03-10 - Product: Agreed to add window-ID hashes to telemetry in release gateway-2.49.0 to improve triage of future events.
